report.clinical_summary: A 60-year-old woman with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) reports persistent fatigue, recurrent infections, and occasional bruising. She takes 420 mg ibrutinib once daily after breakfast and has developed a consistent routine. She has a collaborative care team including primary care physician, hematologist, and oncologist. She describes her illness as chronic and lifelong, integrated into her identity, with significant impact on work and social functioning. She expresses high concern about future uncertainty and emotional struggle, though she trusts her healthcare team and believes her medications are essential.
